gaps: Every breath-one trade was written as two parties and a return path: a power goes over, something comes back, and the question was whether the power can be traded back. Pressing on the carrier in Fence around the process showed that the no-shop returns the paper and not the power, since the power lived in the bidders' heat and the clause never held it; and the exchanged hostage refused to sit still, since a body valued by its giver acquires a lever of its own. This produced the changed question for breath two: where does a traded power actually go, and does the trade conserve it at all.
accepted: Card for one meeting: holders lend their votes to an activist by proxy card, giving the exercise of the vote and receiving a campaign they did not have to run; the carrier is the card, good for one meeting and revoked by any later-dated card up to the hour of the vote, so the power returns by its own clock with nothing worn off; the rate is zero at the margin, since each lender gives a vote worth nothing alone and the borrower assembles a majority from votes nobody priced; found one-sided when the activist settles with the board for two seats before the vote and the lenders learn their votes were the borrower's bargaining chip and never their ballot; not a sale, since the vote never leaves the share.

Seat for the check: an investor gives capital and receives one director's vote of five and the information that comes with the room; the carrier is the investors' rights agreement, which conditions the seat on holding a threshold of shares and sunsets it at a listing, so the seat lapses back by the paper; the rate is lumpy, since the last dollar across the threshold buys the whole seat and every dollar after it buys nothing, which is why the lead fights over the threshold and not the price; not control, and the investor who thought it bought control discovers this at the first vote that goes four to one, while the founder discovers what a seat is at the first vote that goes three to two.

Fence around the process: a founder gives the power to run an auction for thirty days and receives a term sheet whose only binding clause is the fence; the carrier is the no-shop together with the other bidders' calendars, and the clause returns the power on its date, but the power was never in the clause, it lived in the bidders' heat, and bidders told to wait find other deals, so an auction paused does not resume at the temperature it was paused at; the rate is written as thirty days and paid as the auction, and the party inside the fence can lower its price in the last week knowing this; not a breakup fee, which prices the walk, since the fence prices nothing and consumes the alternative.

Leased strike: a union gives the strike for the term of the contract and receives binding arbitration of grievances, a procedure that makes the employer obey a third party's answer; the carrier is the agreement and the arbitrator; the rate is flat across the term though the strike's value peaks in the employer's busy season, and arbitration pays out at the pace of the docket; the power returns at expiry in law, but a strike not run in twenty years returns as a threat the employer no longer believes and the members no longer know how to run, so what is leased comes back lighter each term; not ghost leverage, an obsolete power still obeyed, but a live one atrophied by disuse, since an employer that tests it may find it still works.

Customs house: a state gives foreign creditors the power to collect its customs and receives a loan, as the Ottoman Public Debt Administration from 1881 and the Dominican receivership of 1905 put creditors' clerks at the revenue's source; the carrier is the receivership itself, an occupation of the place where the money enters; the rate is set by the lender's model of default and not by what the state thinks its sovereignty is worth, so the power is priced as a yield; the loan has a maturity and the receivership has none, so the power returns only by an act of expulsion the carrier never wrote, which the debtor must some decade find the strength to perform; not conditionality, which binds by the next tranche and can be dropped by dropping the tranche.

Veto sold as an improbability: a founder gives an investor class consent rights over named future states, a sale below a price, a new financing, a change to the charter, and receives a higher valuation now; the carrier is the charter's protective provisions, held by class vote; the rate is set by the founder's estimate of how unlikely those states are, so the veto is sold at the price of an improbability and exercised at the price of a certainty, and the buyer, who has seen a hundred companies reach those states, knows the base rate better than the seller who has seen one; found one-sided the day the improbable arrives and the acqui-hire that would save the team needs a signature from a class that would receive nothing; not control, since a veto can keep a future from happening and cannot make one happen.

Drag for tag: a minority gives the majority the power to force its shares into a sale and receives the right to join any sale the majority makes; the carrier is the shareholders' agreement; the rate is symmetric in the text and asymmetric in frequency, since drags fire at nearly every exit and tags almost never, because majorities rarely sell in part, so a swap of two powers over two futures is priced as if the futures were equally likely and pays out as if only one existed; found one-sided when the drag fires at a price the majority's preference makes handsome and the minority's common makes nothing. Adds to impasse-inventions' swap of vetoes the shape of the rate: a power-for-power swap is priced by which future arrives, not by the powers' text.

First look that chills the room: a founder gives an investor the right to match or lead the next round and receives a better price now; the carrier is the clause; the rate is written as an option and paid as a chill, since outsiders will not spend a month of diligence on a round they can be matched out of, so what was given was not a first look but the outsiders' willingness to bid; found one-sided when the next process is run and the serious bidders decline to come, and returned only by a waiver the holder can sell a second time; not the fence, which consumes a process already running, since the first look keeps the next one from starting. Adds to impasse-inventions' right of first refusal the mechanism by which the right is worth more than its text.

Silence on the tab: a reporter or an analyst gives the power to publish, one item at a time, and receives access; the carrier is the repeated game, since access is revocable at any moment and silence must be bought again at every story; the rate ratchets, because each story withheld is an investment in the relationship that a disclosure would forfeit, so the price of the next disclosure rises with every one not made; found one-sided when the access yields only what cannot be printed and the power to publish has quietly become a power to know; not discretion sold as a good, a single sale, but a lease whose rent rises with the tenancy.

Hostage returned as partisan: two parties each give the other a power to punish them through a body they value, as in the medieval exchange of sons and the hostages Rome took from client kings, and each receives the same hold over the other; the carrier is the body together with the giver's continuing love for it, since a hostage the giver stops valuing holds nothing, so the rate is the ratio of the two givers' caring and not the ranks of the persons exchanged; the trade inverts, on the standard reading of Roman practice, when the hostage raised in the holder's house returns as its friend, so the giver gave a hold and got back a party of the other side; not the ugly hostage of who-can-be-bound, a token worth nothing to its holder and posted one way, since this hold is mutual and its product changes sides.

Name on the door: a partner gives share and receives the name on the letterhead, and a founder gives the chief executive's chair and receives the chairman's; the power given is a share of decisions and profits, the thing received is a sign, and the carrier is the sign plus whoever routes through it; the rate is settled afterward by third parties, since a sign that captures a flow, the client who will deal only with the named partner, the press that calls the founder, regenerates the substance it was traded for, while a sign that captures no flow decays into a room where the meetings are held elsewhere; found one-sided on the day one learns which kind one holds; not a status conversion, which turns one standing into another in the same holder, since here the substance passes to a counterparty and outsiders set what the sign is worth.

Sword for quarter: the party that surrenders gives its residual power to fight and receives quarter; the carrier is the ceremony and the law that makes a prisoner a status rather than a corpse; the rate is set by what the residual resistance would cost the victor, so the garrison that can still make the siege expensive gets terms and the one that cannot gets none, which is why terms must be asked while the walls still stand; consumed in the giving, since the disarmed cannot rearm and the victor's side of the trade is enforced only by the victor's own need for the next surrender; the wolf that shows the throat gives the same thing at a rate set by the winner's need for a pack; not deference, which is given again each morning and can be withheld tomorrow.

residue.item: Go-between's toll: two parties who cannot speak each hand a mediator the power to carry, sequence, and frame their words, and the mediator's power grows with every message.
residue.why: Held to breath two: as a rate it is Silence on the tab (a price that ratchets with every exchange), and the neutral holder is already in impasse-inventions; what remained, a power minted in a party that did not sit at the table, was resolved in breath two as Key man's lever rather than admitted here.

residue.item: Tribute for immunity: a regular payment given for harm withheld.
residue.why: Rejected: already cooperation-mechanisms' Regularized tribute for immunity from predation, and what moves is money, not power, so it fails the item type.

residue.item: Swap of vetoes over different domains.
residue.why: Merged into Drag for tag: the swap itself is an impasse-invention already; what the fieldwork adds, that a power-for-power swap is priced by which future arrives and not by the powers' text, is carried by Drag for tag's rate shape.

residue.item: Burned bridge: a party destroys its own retreat and receives a stronger bargaining position.
residue.why: Rejected against the item type: nothing is received from a counterparty, so a precommitment trades with the world rather than with a party; it belongs to the leverage maps and is named in the boundary claims.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real term sheet or treaty runs several of these trades at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.
The seriation is an itinerary of what becomes of the given power, not a ranking of danger, value, or historical order; the map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (the Ottoman and Dominican receiverships, Roman hostages, proffer practice, dual-class charters, junior coalition partners) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific histories; Hostage returned as partisan and Kingmaker's tax rest on contested readings and say so in the item.
Trades of money for goods, and of money for a single exercise of a power (the bribe, the fee for a decision), are outside: no power moves, only an outcome.

Powers a party trades with itself or with the world (the burned bridge, the Ulysses contract, the precommitment) are outside, since nothing is received from a counterparty; they belong to the leverage maps.

gaps: The changed question yielded a power that cannot be passed on because its carrier kills it in transit (Vote that dies in transit), two powers consumed by routes other than the sword's, the fact copied so that exclusivity dies (Queen for a day) and the source spent while the power comes back (Kingmaker's tax), a sign that draws the summons rather than the client (Blame-bearer's fee), and a trade between two that mints a power in a third (Key man's lever). The territory pointer 'power trades' stands, but the of-sentence now carries what becomes of the given power, and the live question 'which powers can be traded back' resolved into a test: a power returns intact only when its carrier is the power, and a trade need not conserve power at all.
accepted: Vote that dies in transit: the public gives its vote and receives the position, a share at a measured small discount, while the founder keeps ten votes a share; the carrier is the charter, which converts high-vote shares to one vote when they leave the founder's hands, so the founder's control is a power that cannot be sold onward, only held, and passes by sunset clause or by death; the rate is the dual-class discount, a few percent off for the vote given up; found one-sided when the founder's judgment goes and nothing but the calendar can retrieve the vote; not the proxy card, which lends a vote that survives the lending, since this is a vote the carrier kills to keep it from being lent at all.

Blame-bearer's fee: a principal gives the visible power, the signature on the filing, the name in the registry, the responsible person on the license, and receives invisibility, while a nominee gives its name and receives a fee; the carrier is the registry that names the nominee, so the summons goes where the registry points; the rate prices the ordinary year, and the liability that arrives in the rare one was never priced, since the fee is set as if the nominee's name were only a name; found one-sided when the liability arrives and the nominee learns that the decision was never theirs and the answer for it is; not the name on the door, whose sign draws clients, since this sign draws process servers.

Queen for a day: a witness gives what it knows and receives use immunity under a proffer letter, which bars the prosecutor from using the words themselves; the carrier is the letter; the witness's power was the exclusivity of the fact, and it is consumed by the telling, since a fact once on the record is a record and not a lever, so the trade must be struck before the fact is spoken and the price can only fall after; found one-sided when derivative use arrives, the leads the words opened being chargeable though the words are not; not the sword, whose carrier passes to the victor, since here the carrier is copied and what dies is being the only one who holds it.

Kingmaker's tax: a small party gives its votes in the chamber and receives ministries, at a rate set by pivotality and not by size, so five seats that complete a majority buy more than forty that do not; the carrier is the coalition agreement and the confidence vote; the trade consumes not the power given but its source, since on a common reading the junior partner's voters, who elected it to be an alternative, punish it for having been a government, so the votes return at the next election and the electorate does not; not the veto, which keeps a future from happening, since the kingmaker makes one happen and is billed for it.

Key man's lever: investors in a fund give their commitment and receive the power to suspend the fund's investing if named partners leave; the carrier is the limited partnership agreement; the rate looks cheap to the firm, which does not plan to lose the named, but the trade mints a power in a hand that did not sit at the table, since each named partner now holds a lever over its own firm, leaving triggers the suspension, and can price its staying at every renegotiation; the firm's power over its own partners is what was quietly sold; found one-sided when a named partner asks for more carry with the agreement open on the table; not a hostage, who is held, since the key man holds.

residue.item: Escrowed power: both sides give a neutral the power to release code or funds on a condition neither can trigger alone.
residue.why: Rejected: restates impasse-inventions' neutral holder, and the neutral's power is scripted by the deposit rather than minted by it, which is what makes it a deposit and not a trade.

residue.item: Hand that cannot close: a client gives a lawyer, priest, or physician a hold over itself, what it knows, to a party the privilege forbids to squeeze.
residue.why: Unresolved seed: strange and possibly fertile, but as written it is who-can-be-bound's hold reversed, given rather than taken, and nothing is received in power; it needs a mechanism by which the privilege's failure (waiver, the crime-fraud exception) turns the deposit into a trade before admission.

residue.item: Ulysses at the mast: a party gives a future self's power to a present rule.
residue.why: Rejected: no counterparty, a trade with oneself, and excluded by the same boundary claim as the burned bridge.

residue.item: Apprentice's deference: the junior gives the power to contest and receives instruction.
residue.why: Rejected: carried by status-conversions' Practice given to the trusted and Furniture's ear; the power-trade reading adds only that deference is re-given daily, which Sword for quarter's discriminator already uses.

residue.item: Go-between's toll: two parties who cannot speak each hand a mediator the power to carry, sequence, and frame their words, and the mediator's power grows with every message.
residue.why: Rejected after being held from breath one: decomposes into Key man's lever (a power minted in a hand that did not sit at the table) and Silence on the tab (a rate that ratchets with every exchange); the only difference left, that the go-between was chosen by both sides, is a fact about the carrier rather than a new mechanism.

neighbors.left: Sword for quarter: the party that surrenders gives its residual power to fight and receives quarter; the carrier is the ceremony and the law that makes a prisoner a status rather than a corpse; the rate is set by what the residual resistance would cost the victor, so the garrison that can still make the siege expensive gets terms and the one that cannot gets none, which is why terms must be asked while the walls still stand; consumed in the giving, since the disarmed cannot rearm and the victor's side of the trade is enforced only by the victor's own need for the next surrender; the wolf that shows the throat gives the same thing at a rate set by the winner's need for a pack; not deference, which is given again each morning and can be withheld tomorrow.
neighbors.right: Queen for a day: a witness gives what it knows and receives use immunity under a proffer letter, which bars the prosecutor from using the words themselves; the carrier is the letter; the witness's power was the exclusivity of the fact, and it is consumed by the telling, since a fact once on the record is a record and not a lever, so the trade must be struck before the fact is spoken and the price can only fall after; found one-sided when derivative use arrives, the leads the words opened being chargeable though the words are not; not the sword, whose carrier passes to the victor, since here the carrier is copied and what dies is being the only one who holds it.
neighbors.separating_case: A defector who comes over with a pistol and the address of the safe house: handing over the pistol is the sword, consumed because the carrier passes, and the defector keeps every fact and can price each one separately afterward; giving the address is the proffer, consumed because the fact is now a record, and the defector keeps every weapon. Each power is consumed by a different route and a party can spend one while holding the other, so surrender and disclosure do not collapse into one item.

checks.boundary_case: A bribe, money for a decision, is out: the official exercises the power in the payer's favor and keeps it, so nothing moves but the outcome, and the same official can be bought again tomorrow by someone else. Seat for the check is in on exactly that contrast, since the vote itself changes hands and the buyer can cast it against the seller. Buying a controlling stake is the tempting middle case and is kept out as a goods trade in which power comes bundled with ownership; the map's terms (drag, veto, first look, super-vote) are in because each unbundles a power from the shares and prices it alone.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the sequence conceals: Fence around the process → First look that chills the room → Fence around the process, where each round's exclusivity lowers the price of the next round's exclusivity, so a founder who reads the itinerary as one trade at a time never sees the ratchet. It shows an incompatibility at Veto sold as an improbability → Drag for tag, two powers each sold as improbable that collide in the same improbable state, where only one can hold. It shows a fork at Name on the door → Blame-bearer's fee, the same signature branching by which third parties route through it. It shows two passages between levels: Leased strike → Sword for quarter, where a power returned lighter each term is at some term indistinguishable from a power consumed, and Hostage returned as partisan → Key man's lever, where a power that returns inverted is seen to have minted a third party's power along the way. And Card for one meeting → Vote that dies in transit shows a dependency between the two ends of the itinerary: the market for lending votes exists only among votes that survive transfer, so the founder's super-vote is excluded from the proxy market by the same carrier that keeps it.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each admitted item names a distinct power given, a distinct thing received, a carrier, a rate shape, and a moment of unwinding or discovery, and the strange members (a paper that returns without the power, a hostage who comes back for the other side, a sign that draws the summons, a vote that dies if it moves, a fact consumed by telling, a trade that arms a third) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into advice about reading term sheets carefully.

next_crossfield_opening: Powers minted by a trade between others: connect Key man's lever with witness-architectures' Deputized injury (a harm registers only once a bearer entitled to bring it exists) and with passages-between-levels; ask which trades create a party rather than move a power, and whether a minted power can be bought back by the two who minted it without the third's consent.
